take_homes: Don't hand people the agent. Pick the shape that moves their outcome: for my team that's shared context files, one copy that everyone builds on.
The people plan stalls on names. An empty owner slot is the finding, and it tells me what to fix first.
Ask what would have to be true for Mikko to drop his spreadsheet before I build anything for him.

monday.move: Talk to Mikko about how he does the usage-pricing analysis today, test one switch assumption, and ask who should own a shared context folder for the pricing pilot.
monday.who: Mikko (pricing analyst), then the head of pricing for the owner question
monday.stop_condition: If Mikko's current way of working is good enough and he wouldn't switch, I drop the candidate and change it. I don't push.
monday.blocker: Nobody owns a shared place for the context files, and everyone keeps their own copy.

misconception.why: I still think prompts matter. But the point that the work lives in curated memory and corrections, not in the instructions file, means better prompts won't get my team of fourteen working. Shared context and a named owner will.

one_line: The exercises were useful and gave me a named Monday move, but the lecture repeats the big idea twice and I skimmed half of it.
